title: performance canary: automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add automated perf canary detector and rollout guards for latency and throughput regressions. This PR implements a continuous canary pipeline that runs lightweight microbenchmarks on candidate model and runtime changes, detects regressions using adaptive thresholds and hysteresis, and ties detection events to rollout guard actions (pause rollout, automatic rollback to previous model variant, and alerting). Motivation: we've seen a recurring class of incidents where subtle scheduler/kernel changes cause 5-15% p99 latency regressions in tail workloads during canary rollouts. This change introduces (1) a detector service that consumes canary metrics, computes relative regressions vs baseline using a bootstrap-based significance test and configurable hysteresis, (2) a policy engine that maps detection outcomes to rollout actions with rate-limited automated rollback and manual approval paths, (3) integration with the perf-canary canary runner to run representative latency/throughput traces and prefix caching scenarios, (4) observability: new dashboards, perf regression histograms, and dedicated alerting channels, and (5) an expanded test harness including deterministic perf sims and CI canary integration. Important notes: thresholds are configurable per-model and per-hardware-class, detector uses a 95% confidence bootstrap with a minimum sample window to avoid noisy flips, hysteresis requires two consecutive detection windows before automated rollback unless severity exceeds 20% p99 increase or throughput drops >15%. Rollout guard actions are recorded in audit logs and emit structured events for Redwood Console to display. This PR includes new schema changes to canary metadata (canary_config.v2) — migration is backward compatible and gated behind a feature flag. The description below includes the checklist and how to validate in staging. Checklist: - [x] detector service implemented and unit tested - [x] policy engine implemented and unit tested - [x] canary runner integration updated - [x] dashboards + alerts wired - [x] migration behind feature flag - [x] e2e perf sims added - [x] docs updated (internal runbooks) How to validate in staging: enable feature flag perf_canary_v2, deploy service to staging, run the canary runner against a short sequence (see test harness), validate detector triggers on synthetic regressions injected via canary runner, confirm rollout pauses/rollbacks and events in console, and monitor alert channel. Related: ENG-4823 (design), ENG-4901 (canary runner refactor).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Looks good overall. Two questions: 1) how do we protect against false positives during noisy windows? 2) can we make the rollback window configurable per-customer?

Aisha Patel: For noise we have a min-sample-window and bootstrap stat with 95% CI; also hysteresis requires two detection windows to auto-rollback by default. Rollback window is configurable per-model and per-tenant via canary_config.v2; documented in runbook.
